issues.description: The problem statement and UML describe a Stock class and instruct students to use a static Stock stock in SealSaloon, but the template repository provides a fully implemented Inventory class (with the expected methods) and an empty Stock.java. The solution also uses Inventory (static Inventory stock) instead of Stock. This name/type mismatch between 'Stock' and 'Inventory' is structural and will confuse students about which class to use and whether they must implement Stock or use the provided Inventory.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock, or (B) provide a concrete Stock implementation in the template (or rename Inventory.java to Stock.java and remove the empty Stock.java). Ensure the SealSaloon specification and templates both use the same type name for the shared stock.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (the shared inventory used by SealSaloon), but the provided template and reference solution use a class named 'Inventory' to provide the same API (add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock). This mismatch between 'Stock' (problem text/UML) and 'Inventory' (code) is likely to confuse students: they may search for or attempt to implement a 'Stock' class while the starter code and solution already provide the functionality under the name 'Inventory'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Either (a) rename the Inventory class/file in the template and solution to Stock (and update references), or (b) update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock'. Ensure any empty Stock.java file in the template/solution is removed or populated to avoid ambiguity.
